extraction_warnings: This paper does not include the actual content of Supplementary Tables S1, S2, S4, or S5, which likely contain per-sample/per-subject metadata (e.g., individual ages, sex, country, accession numbers) for the >1,000 genomes and >6,500 metagenomes analyzed; only aggregate cohort-level statistics for the three newly sequenced non-Westernized cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania) are given in the main text.

Because only aggregate statistics (mean, SD, range, % sex) are reported for cohorts, granularity was set to subgroup_level (cohort x age-group) rather than sample_level, per instructions not to invent per-sample rows from aggregates.
The 'sex' field is an enum requiring a single value per entry, but most subgroups report mixed-sex percentages; only the 100%-female Ethiopia adult subgroup could be confidently assigned.

'age_group' classification is derived from mean age only; actual reported age ranges for some subgroups (e.g., Ghana children 0-15 yrs, Ethiopia infants 0.167-4.5 yrs) span multiple schema age_group categories.
pmid was taken from the provided paper_id tag rather than being explicitly stated within the paper body text.
study_name, subject_id, sample_id, curator, ancestry, family identifiers, and antibiotics exclusion criteria were not found anywhere in the provided text.

This paper is primarily a microbial genomics study (Prevotella copri); most clinical/host-phenotype schema fields (zygosity, BMI, treatment, tumor staging, obstetric/neonatal fields, HLA, smoking, etc.) are not addressed and were marked not_reported.

Age and sex data are reported only as subgroup-level summary statistics (mean, SD, range) for six cohort/age-group combinations (Ghana adults/children, Ethiopia adults/infants, Tanzania adults/children), not per-individual; granularity set to subgroup_level accordingly.
Disease status ('Healthy', free of self-reported disease) applies uniformly to all three non-Westernized cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania) described in Experimental Model and Subject Details.

Other cohorts described in the paper (public metagenomic datasets, disease case-control datasets for CRC/T2D/IBD/etc., ancient samples) do not have explicit per-subject demographic/clinical metadata reported in the main text sections extracted here.
